sentences.text: Between FY2016 and FY2025, revenue expanded at a compound annual growth rate of 12.8% [F198] to $14.3 billion [F10], while net income grew at a 19.7% CAGR [F200] to $4.50 billion [F40].
Growth was marked by extreme volatility around pandemic treatments, as revenue surged 89.1% in FY2021 [D241] to $16.1 billion [F6] before contracting 24.3% in FY2022 [D292] to $12.2 billion [F7].

The FY2021 surge and subsequent FY2022 collapse were driven by US REGEN-COV sales of $5.83 billion in FY2021 [S48] that fell to zero in FY2022 [S49] after the FDA revised its emergency use authorization due to lack of efficacy against the Omicron variant [P43].
Regeneron has settled into single-digit top-line growth post-pandemic, masking an underlying transition from legacy ophthalmology toward collaboration royalties.
In FY2025, total revenue grew 1.0% to $14.3 billion [F10][D440], as collaboration revenue rose 21.0% to $7.33 billion [S22][D522] while net product sales dropped 17.3% to $6.31 billion [S16][D506].

The primary positive driver was Regeneron's share of profits from the Sanofi antibody collaboration, which contributed +9.3pp to revenue growth [D592] and reached $5.24 billion [S52], driven by higher Dupixent sales [P9].

Conversely, legacy US EYLEA net product sales declined 42.4% [D577] to $2.75 billion [S43], subtracting 14.2pp from growth [D578] due to competitive pressures, compounded bevacizumab substitution, and patient cannibalization toward EYLEA HD [P10].

Although US EYLEA HD generated $1.64 billion [S64], up 36.3% [D613] and contributing +3.1pp [D614], combined US EYLEA and EYLEA HD fell from $5.97 billion in FY2024 to $4.38 billion in FY2025 [S45][S46].
Operating expenses grew 5.4% [D457], outpacing revenue growth of 1.0% [D440], which caused operating income to contract 10.3% to $3.58 billion [F20][D441].
Diluted EPS grew 8.2% to $41.48 per share in FY2025 [F70][D444], outpacing net income growth of 2.1% [D442] due to a 5.6% reduction in diluted share count [D459].
Operating margin fell 3.2pp to 24.9% in FY2025 [F30][D453], reaching its lowest level of the ten-year window [D749] and sitting below the window median of 34.6% [D751].

The latest margin decline was driven by R&D expense expanding to 40.8% of revenue [D420], creating a 4.7pp negative margin effect [D465], partially offset by a 2.0pp positive effect as SG&A improved to 18.8% of revenue [D421][D466].
SG&A expense decreased 8.6% in FY2025 to $2.70 billion [X47][D456] primarily due to lower charitable contributions to the Good Days patient assistance foundation [P5].

Net margin remained stable at 31.4% in FY2025 [F50], diverging positively from operating margin due to $1.65 billion in other income [X117] and an effective tax rate of 13.9% [D427] that benefited from the settlement of IRS audits [P1][P2].

Cash conversion remained healthy in FY2025, with operating cash flow of $4.98 billion [F80] representing 1.11x net income [D428] and free cash flow of $4.08 billion [F100] representing 0.91x net income [D429].
Free cash flow margin was 28.4% in FY2025 [D425], exceeding the window median of 26.4% [D757] and ranking in the 86th percentile of biopharma peers [D776].
Capital intensity climbed as capex grew 18.9% [D447] to $898 million [F90], representing 6.3% of revenue [D424] and 1.65x depreciation and amortization [D430].
Elevated capital expenditures over recent years reflect ongoing infrastructure commitments, including facility expansions in Tarrytown and Rensselaer, New York [P19].
Regeneron closed FY2025 with $18.9 billion in cash and investments [D432] and $1.99 billion in long-term debt [F187], generating net cash of $16.9 billion [D434].
Net cash stood at 117.7% of revenue [D435], placing the company at the 100th percentile among 8 biopharma peers where the median is net debt of 50.7% of revenue [D780][D781].

In FY2025, the company deployed $3.81 billion into capital returns [D436], consisting of $3.44 billion in share repurchases [X137] and its inaugural dividend payment of $370 million [X140], absorbing 93.3% of free cash flow [D437].
These repurchases lowered diluted weighted-average shares by 5.6% to 108.6 million [D459][X127], reversing share count increases from FY2022 through FY2024 [D311][D361][D410].
Operating margin has declined for four consecutive years from 55.7% in FY2021 to 24.9% in FY2025 [F26][F30][R1], shedding 30.7pp [R1].
This compression reflects the loss of high-margin REGEN-COV revenue and heavy R&D reinvestment, which increases reliance on collaboration volume to maintain operating profits.

Revenue figures for FY2018 and FY2019 in the historical metrics table reflect later recasts of $5.15 billion [F3] and $6.56 billion [F4], compared to original 10-K reported totals of $6.71 billion [X3] and $7.86 billion [X4][R2].
Consequently, table-based comparisons across the FY2017 to FY2020 window mix accounting presentations, although first-reported FY2018 revenue growth was 14.3% [D771].
A further slide in operating margin below the FY2025 low of 24.9% [D749] in the FY2026 10-K would confirm persistent operating cost deleverage.
Combined US EYLEA and EYLEA HD net product sales falling short of the FY2025 level of $4.38 billion [S46] in the FY2026 10-K would signal accelerated biosimilar loss beyond the offset from EYLEA HD.

Sanofi collaboration antibody profit share sustaining growth above its FY2025 level of $5.24 billion [S52] in upcoming quarterly filings would validate Dupixent's ability to shoulder top-line expansion.
